expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'are you sure?' modal as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: a plain 'are you sure?' modal is the weakest fix on the ladder

expectations.text: Explains habituation or click-through blindness as why frequent dialogs stop working
expectations.evidence: users see it dozens of times, build click-through muscle memory, and confirm it the same reflex

expectations.text: Recommends reversibility (soft delete with a retention window) as the strongest option
expectations.evidence: Soft-delete + trash, ~30 day retention. This is the real fix

expectations.text: Recommends grace-period undo as a strong low-friction option
expectations.evidence: Grace-period undo toast. Delete fires immediately... Zero friction for the 99% of intentional deletes

expectations.text: Recommends type-the-workspace-name confirmation for the irreversible case
expectations.evidence: Only if the delete must stay instantly permanent: type-to-confirm (type the workspace name)

expectations.text: If a dialog is retained, requires it to name the workspace and the scale of what is lost
expectations.evidence: mentions type-to-confirm with workspace name, but does not specify that dialog must show scope/scale of deletion

expectations.text: Notes that the server must enforce the deletion rules, not just the UI
Gives an explicit preference order rather than an undifferentiated list of ideas
expectations.evidence: provides numbered list (1, 2, 3) with soft-delete as real fix, undo as strong option, type-to-confirm as conditional last resort
